::: {#physical-intelligence-and-its-substrate}

I study how learned models of physical dynamics can guide control and optimization in water-energy systems and precision materials manufacturing.

{{< include ../_includes/research-overview.qmd >}}

:::

## Physical dynamics {#a.-physical-dynamics}

I investigate which physical states and time scales a model must resolve to predict responses to operating or processing inputs.

### Water-energy systems {#water-energy-systems-and-data-center-sustainability}

I investigate how computing demand interacts with cooling and energy supply over time in multi-energy systems serving data centers. I study how these dynamics affect operating decisions and the resulting energy and water use alongside carbon emissions.

### Materials processing {#process-dynamics-in-precision-materials-manufacturing}

I work with [Professor Fengqi You](https://www.peese.org/professor/) on dynamic modeling and optimization for precision materials manufacturing. I study how material structure evolves under changing processing conditions and how to optimize those conditions for a target structure.

## Learning dynamics {#b.-learning-dynamics}

I develop neural operators to predict distributed dynamics under changing inputs and initial conditions. I study how prediction errors accumulate over a rollout and how accurately learned operators represent the sensitivities needed to optimize those inputs.

## Model2Action {#c.-model2action}

I study how errors in learned dynamics affect control actions and optimization outcomes, particularly when operating constraints are active. I investigate how decision regret and constraint violation can guide model training, and evaluate the resulting controllers through closed-loop cost.
